character_identity_rule: Match the original Sol artwork: recognizable compact reference proportions and volume, asymmetric flame silhouette, original red/orange/cream layer relationships, short rounded arms and tiny stubby feet at their original lengths and attachment points. sources.title: Fire 400 ka — Pathways to Ancient Britain
sources.supports: The research team distinguishes likely use of wildfires and maintained embers from intentional ignition. Early dates are uncertain; no first discoverer is identified.

sources.title: Davis et al. — Earliest evidence of making fire
sources.supports: The study reports evidence interpreted as deliberate fire-making at Barnham around 400,000 years ago. This evidence date is not a known first invention or discoverer.

sources.title: Berna et al. — Fire evidence at Wonderwerk Cave
sources.supports: Burned bone and plant ash document burning in an archaeological context around one million years ago. This does not identify a person or establish the first ignition method.

clips.title: A monkey rubs two sticks and starts a little flame
clips.action: Begin with the two unlit sticks crossed and touching as in the first frame. During0.3–2.2s the monkey playfully rubs their upper lengths together in short back-and-forth strokes, one stick per hand, keeping both grips readable and the wood contact continuous. The sticks remain two distinct objects throughout; no separate prop enters. A faint wisp appears on the rubbed wood, then the upper ends catch little orange flames around2.4s. The monkey stops rubbing, lifts its shoulders and leans back slightly in one surprised reaction by3.2s. End with the same crossed shafts and both small flames attached to the rubbed upper ends shown in the last frame. Retain supported feet and the single tail. Continue a brief natural blink/breath and gentle wood-flame flicker through5s without freezing the whole scene. No extra hand, third stick, grip teleportation, banana, log, huge fire or body/texture ripple. This is a playful imagined cartoon accident, not an asserted historical discovery.

clips.first_frame: The monkey looks down with quiet curiosity and holds exactly TWO SHORT WOODEN STICKS: one stick in its left hand and one in its right hand. Both are held above the ground. The left-hand stick points diagonally up-right; the right-hand stick points diagonally up-left so their exposed wood tips cross and TOUCH in front of the monkey. Both gripping hands are separated, below the crossing, leaving the wood-to-wood contact unobstructed. Include only these two plain brown sticks, each with a simple readable shaft and a few pale frayed wood fibers at the touching point. Neither stick is supported by another piece of wood. The sticks are entirely unlit: no ember, glow, smoke, sparks or flame. The monkey’s face, ears, body, feet and single curved tail match the reference. No banana, no log, no third stick, no bow/drill/fireboard apparatus, no extra hand.
clips.last_frame: Keep the exact same monkey identity, seated body, supported feet, single tail, forest, camera, clear foreground and TWO sticks from the first frame. The rubbed upper ends of BOTH sticks have now caught small orange flames: a larger tongue on the upper-right tip and a smaller tongue on the upper-left tip, attached to the wood with a little local darkening.
